summary: Waterboro's 1918 steel lookout was lost in the 1947 fire and rebuilt in wood in 1948; volunteers have staffed it since state funding ended in 1991.

facts.design: 30-foot treated wood tower with a 13 by 13 foot shingled wood cab (NHLR)

access.note: Opened and closed by the tower steward in 2024; the 2024 report does not say how visitors arrange entry.

visit.trail_note: A foot trail of about 0.4 miles was built from the parking area to the tower, per a 1941 report on Alfred CCC camp work.

events.note: Original 24-foot steel tower erected in the fall of 1918
Wildfire overran the mountain in October; the marker says the tower was destroyed; the 1947 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts says the fire spotter had to leave
Rebuilt in wood: 30 feet tall with a 13 by 13 foot cab
State funding ended; volunteers from the area manned the tower after that
Register gives November 25, 1996; the marker says it was accepted at the August 1997 FFLA conference
Closed for the entire 2016 fire season for lack of volunteers
FFLA restoration grant of $500 awarded for materials to repair braces and cross members on the wooden superstructure
Vandalism; Waterboro firefighters spent a morning repairing damage to the steel lock on the door (WMTW, May 2019)
Volunteers replaced some lower leg ties in October, using lumber donated by Moulton Lumber in Cornish

corrections.why: 7.3 m (24 ft) is the 1918 steel tower that was lost in 1947. The standing tower is the 1948 wooden tower, 30 feet tall per the register and the marker.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1918 steel tower (24 ft) was lost in the 1947 fire; the 1948 wooden tower is the one standing, which is why the register gives 1948 as the built year.

The register gives November 25, 1996, and the marker gives August 1997 for acceptance at the FFLA conference. These may be a listing date and a ceremony date, but no source says which is the registration date.

sources.title: Ossipee Hill Fire Tower Historical Marker
Vandals targeting York County fire tower, officials say

notes_for_editor: Brief's height 7.3 m is the 24-foot 1918 steel tower; the standing tower is 30 feet (9.1 m). Brief's 2018 break-in is not supported: WMTW reports vandalism and firefighter repairs in May 2019, and no 2018 source was found. Brief's 2008 stair repaint has no source found, so it is dropped. Brief's 2019 brace replacement is only the FFLA grant awarded for materials; completion is not confirmed, so the story says the grant was awarded. Unresolved: the watchman's name in the 1947 fire (Mike Ferguson per the marker, Donald Ferguson per the 1947 newspaper quoted by Forest Lookouts), and the register date (1996) versus the marker's 1997 acceptance. Access: how visitors arrange entry is not verified. The 2025 plans for stair work and cab siding are not included.
